sources.entry: MediaMTX - Ready-to-use, zero-dependency real-time media server and proxy to publish, read, record, playback and route video/audio streams over SRT, WebRTC, RTSP, RTMP, HLS, MPEG-TS, RTP. (Source Code, Clients) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: MediaMTX is a zero-dependency, single-executable live media server and proxy that publishes, reads, routes, records and plays back video and audio streams across many protocols.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes MediaMTX as a "media router" that moves real-time video and audio streams from publishers to readers. It accepts publishing over Media-over-QUIC, SRT, WebRTC, RTSP, RTMP, HLS, MPEG-TS and RTP, and serves reading over Media-over-QUIC, SRT, WebRTC, RTSP, RTMP and HLS. Streams are automatically converted between protocols, and several streams can be served at once on separate paths. Streams can be recorded to disk in fMP4 or MPEG-TS format and played back, and always-available streams can be served even when the publisher is offline. The server can also forward streams to other servers, proxy requests, authenticate users (internal, HTTP or JWT), be controlled through a Control API, expose Prometheus-compatible metrics, and run hooks on connect, disconnect, read or publish events. Configuration can be hot-reloaded without disconnecting existing clients.
use_cases: relay RTSP camera feeds to browsers via WebRTC or HLS
convert RTMP from OBS Studio into HLS or SRT for viewers
record live camera streams to disk in fMP4 or MPEG-TS
forward a live stream to another media server
add authentication in front of live video streams
monitor streaming server CPU and memory with Prometheus
notable: Single executable with no dependencies or interpreter needed
Automatic protocol conversion between supported streaming protocols
Hot reloading of configuration without dropping existing clients
Always-available streams that keep serving when the publisher is offline
Recording and playback of streams from disk
caveats: The README excerpt provided does not include installation or run instructions; see the linked Install and Documentation pages
Supported platforms are stated as Linux, Windows and macOS
